patches.old: This article addresses adaptive event-triggered control for interval type-2 (IT-2) fuzzy cyber-physical systems (CPSs) affected by stochastic deception attacks and Markov-type actuator failures. Since nonlinear CPSs face cyber-layer attacks as well as physical-layer component failures, while their communication resources are often limited, an adaptive event-triggered mechanism (AETM) is employed to reduce redundant network transmissions through dynamic adjustment of the triggering threshold based on real-time state-error information. Specifically, stochastic deception attacks are characterized by a Bernoulli process, and actuator failures are modeled by Markov switching fault matrices. Accordingly, a unified closed-loop model is established. Then, a looped functional dependent on fuzzy membership functions (FMFs) is constructed to exploit membership-function information and sampled-data dynamics. Based on this functional, stability criteria are obtained to guarantee asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system while achieving a prescribed $\mathrm{H}_\infty$ disturbance attenuation level. Moreover, joint design of the controller gains and adaptive triggering parameters is formulated through tractable linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Validation is finally carried out with an engineering-motivated permanent magnet synchronous motor example and a numerical IT-2 fuzzy system to demonstrate the effectiveness and feasibility of the developed method.
patches.new: This article addresses adaptive event-triggered control for interval type-2 (IT-2) fuzzy cyber-physical systems (CPSs) subject to stochastic deception attacks and Markov-type actuator failures. An adaptive event-triggered mechanism (AETM) adjusts the transmission threshold using state-error information to reduce redundant communication. Deception attacks are described by a Bernoulli process, and actuator failures are represented by Markov switching fault matrices. These components are incorporated into a unified closed-loop model. The signs of the membership-function derivatives define operational regions for a region-dependent fuzzy controller. Within this framework, the controller gains and event-triggering weight matrices are jointly designed. A two-sided looped functional dependent on fuzzy membership functions (FMFs) incorporates membership information and sampled-data dynamics. Sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability with a prescribed $\mathrm{H}_\infty$ disturbance attenuation level are formulated as linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). A permanent magnet synchronous motor example and a numerical IT-2 fuzzy example illustrate the control responses and the reduction in data transmissions.

patches.new: The considered impairments affect different but interconnected parts of the closed loop. Deception attacks may corrupt the sampled information used by the controller, whereas actuator failures change the effectiveness of the control input applied to the plant. Event-triggered transmission reduces communication by retaining the last transmitted sample between releases, so the controller must also accommodate the resulting sampling error. Their simultaneous presence therefore motivates a joint analysis of closed-loop stability and disturbance attenuation under the specified attack, failure, and transmission models.

patches.new: Recent studies provide closely related developments under different modeling and control settings. Liu et al.\ \cite{liuTorusEventBased2025} investigated discrete-time IT-2 fuzzy systems under deception attacks using a two-threshold torus-event-triggering protocol and sliding-mode control. Chandrasekar et al.\ \cite{chandrasekarAdaptiveEvent2026} considered adaptive event-triggered asynchronous control of uncertain IT-2 fuzzy Markov jump systems under deception attacks, with a hidden Markov model describing the plant--controller mode mismatch. The attack/failure combination has also been studied: Chen et al.\ \cite{chenProbabilisticEventTriggeredPolicy2023} addressed extended dissipative finite-time control of Markov jump systems under cyberattacks and actuator failures using a probabilistic event-triggered policy. These studies connect communication scheduling, information security, and actuator reliability. The present formulation instead concerns continuous-time IT-2 fuzzy CPSs with Bernoulli deception attacks and Markov-type actuator effectiveness, and uses membership-function derivative signs to organize regional controller gains and triggering weight matrices within a two-sided FMF-dependent looped-functional synthesis. This comparison identifies the particular formulation and design structure studied here; it does not imply that joint attack/failure modeling or adaptive event triggering is itself new.

patches.old: When the triggering error is small, the update of $\delta(t)$ is weakened, thereby avoiding unnecessary fluctuations of the threshold and reducing redundant data transmissions.
patches.new: When the triggering error is small, the update of $\delta(t)$ is weakened. For $\delta(t)>0$ and nonzero triggering error, \eqref{eq:adaptive_law} gives an increasing threshold when $\delta(t)<1/\sigma$ and a decreasing threshold when $\delta(t)>1/\sigma$; its derivative is zero when the error is zero or the threshold equals $1/\sigma$. For fixed sampled state, error, and weighting matrix, a larger threshold makes the inequality in \eqref{eq:Event_TR_1} harder to satisfy. Actual release instants depend on the joint evolution of the sampled state, sampling error, and threshold, and cannot be inferred from the equilibrium value alone.

The endpoint property $V_p(t_k^j)=V_p(t_k^{j+1})=0$ for $p=2,3,4$ permits these auxiliary terms to describe intersample evolution while preserving the endpoint matching used in the analysis. The control-input trajectory shows the transient actuation and its subsequent decay as the states in Fig.~\ref{fig11} approach the origin. The plot does not attribute every input variation solely to a regional switch, since the control law also depends on the received sample, memberships, and actuator mode. patches.old: This study has addressed adaptive event-triggered $\mathrm{H}_{\infty}$ control of IT-2 fuzzy CPSs affected simultaneously by stochastic deception attacks and Markov-type actuator failures. An AETM has been employed to limit unnecessary data transmissions by updating the triggering threshold online using real-time state-error information. In addition, a region-dependent piecewise fuzzy control strategy has been developed by incorporating derivative information from the membership functions. Based on an FMF-dependent and time-dependent looped functional, stability criteria have been obtained to guarantee closed-loop asymptotic stability while achieving a prescribed $\mathrm{H}_{\infty}$ disturbance attenuation level. The controller gains and adaptive event-triggering weight matrices have been jointly determined through tractable LMIs, while a bounding technique has been employed to address the norm-bounded uncertainty induced by Markov-type actuator failures.
patches.new: This study has considered adaptive event-triggered $\mathrm{H}_{\infty}$ control of IT-2 fuzzy CPSs subject to stochastic deception attacks and Markov-type actuator failures. The AETM updates its threshold using state-error information to reduce redundant transmissions. Membership-function derivative information defines operational regions for the fuzzy control design. An FMF-dependent looped functional is used to formulate sufficient stability and performance conditions. The controller gains and event-triggering weight matrices are jointly determined through LMIs, with a bounding technique used to handle actuator-failure uncertainty.

patches.old: An engineering-motivated PMSM example and a numerical IT-2 fuzzy example have demonstrated the effectiveness and applicability of the developed method. Further research will extend the current IT-2 fuzzy control methodology to observer-based output feedback control, since not all system states are measurable in practical industrial applications. Secure control under more sophisticated cyberattack scenarios, such as DoS attacks, and practical network constraints, such as partially unknown Markov transition probabilities, also deserve further investigation.
patches.new: The PMSM and numerical IT-2 fuzzy examples illustrate closed-loop responses and transmission savings under the selected settings. The present analysis uses state feedback, Bernoulli-modeled deception attacks satisfying the specified signal bound, and Markov-type actuator failures with known transition rates. Its theoretical conclusions apply under these assumptions. Observer-based output feedback is a future direction for applications without full-state measurements. DoS attacks and partially unknown Markov transition rates require additional modeling and analysis and are also left for future work.
